s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution
salient_findings: Intensely pruritic skin lesions on anterior thighs
Lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and purpuric edges
Symmetric, mirror-image distribution on anterior thighs
key_facts: 6-year-old girl with no relevant medical history
Lesions resolve spontaneously without residual injury
No preceding infection, topical exposures, sunburn, bites, animal contacts, or recent medications
Laboratory studies are within normal limits

differentials: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands
per_call: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution

shortlist.label: Annular erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, central clearing, and purpuric edges

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Lesions are well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with central clearing

shortlist.label: Urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: Intensely pruritic skin lesions with recurrent 3-day outbreaks

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric edges and symmetric distribution of lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing, which is more characteristic of Erythema annulare centrifugum than Urticaria.

rejected.label: Urticaria
rejected.why: Lesions do not have the typical wheal and flare appearance of Urticaria

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Lesions lack the characteristic target lesions of Erythema multiforme

rejected.label: Annular erythema
rejected.why: Annular erythema is a broader term that does not specifically match the patient's lesion morphology

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: Laboratory studies do not show evidence of vasculitis, such as elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate or C-reactive protein
